claims.text: Temperature changes induce short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range order creates nanoscale domains with distinct lattice parameters.
The nanoscale domains have thermal expansion behavior different from that of the surrounding matrix.
Pre-aging at 600–800 °C promotes local atomic ordering.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between ordered regions and the matrix generates internal stresses during thermal cycling.
The mismatch-generated internal stresses alter dislocation mobility.
The proposed internal stresses alter the alloy's elastic moduli.
The proposed internal stresses alter high-temperature creep behavior.
SRO-induced internal stresses provide a common mechanism for the reported creep, elastic-modulus, and hardening phenomena.
Pre-aged samples will exhibit anomalous lattice-parameter shifts at lower temperatures than homogenized samples without pre-aging.
Pre-aged samples will exhibit greater strain heterogeneity during thermal cycling than homogenized samples without pre-aging.
Pre-aged samples will have a higher creep rate at 1250 °C than homogenized samples without pre-aging.
The homogenized samples without pre-aging will display uniform thermal expansion.
Measurements near 600 °C and 800 °C are expected to capture SRO-associated lattice-parameter changes.
Precipitation or dynamic recovery could produce nanoscale signatures that are difficult to distinguish from SRO-related lattice distortions.
The comparison will use otherwise matched pre-aged and homogenized samples during in-situ diffraction thermal cycling.
Absence of statistically significant differences in lattice expansion, strain heterogeneity, and creep rate, or absence of detectable SRO, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
